title: Seasonal adjustment retained a positive spatial-temperature response in Northeast Shelf zooplankton
abstract: We tested whether seasonal timing can explain strong thermal tracking in Northeast Shelf plankton. We used EcoMon records in 1992-2023, with 14,727 selected zooplankton tows and 8,939 fish-larva tows. We trained spatial temperature and seasonal composition vectors on 1992-2007 data outside each focal spatial block. We then tested later composition change. The coefficient of the frozen spatial warming prediction was 0.610 for zooplankton and 0.668 for fish larvae. A single timing shift changed little. With six separate seasonal shifts, coefficients were 0.599 (conditional 95% crossed-bootstrap interval 0.183-0.898) and 0.460 (-0.084 to 0.891). November-December supplied 91% of signed temperature alignment in fish larvae, versus 39% in zooplankton, but these shares were uncertain. Early spatial and seasonal directions validated outside training blocks. Presence and Hellinger checks retained the main pattern. Odd-even year changes had low repeatability, so raw displacement shares must not be read as causal climate fractions. The test strengthens the zooplankton contrast with weak thermal tracking elsewhere. It leaves a less certain fish-larva contrast. The method does not distinguish advection, demographic replacement or species-specific phenology. One shelf, coarse taxa, sparse seasonal training and observational gradients limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes and external-data reproduction instructions are supplied.

display.caption: The zooplankton spatial-temperature coefficient stayed positive after six seasonal shifts. The fish-larva coefficient was less certain. Bars in the left panel show conditional crossed-bootstrap intervals. The right panel shows point estimates of each season's share of the signed temperature-alignment numerator, not fractions of all change. November-December concentration was uncertain. Early training uses 1992-2007; later changes use 2008-2023.
